text:
maya (PM): Post-launch quick triage thread. Two customer issues + a few small polish asks. Need to sort P0/P1 and whether to ship in the upcoming window. Can we be pragmatic?
ryan (eng): TL;DR: one functional regression (Customer X conversions drop with long contexts) and intermittent embed latency spikes for Customer Y. Also a couple small UX nit requests from beta users.
emma (CS): Customer X reports conversion drop ~12% during long interactions. They flagged it as blocking for their end-to-end flow. Offering a workaround is painful for them.
zara (eng-sre): embed latency spikes look like backpressure in the batching layer during a specific traffic pattern. Short-term: tweak batch timeout + increase worker retry budget. Medium: rework batch allocator. Short-term estimate 2 dev-days + 0.5 infra-day.
tony (design): nits are microcopy changes and spacing + keyboard focus fix. ~2 design hours + ~4 dev hours if picked up now. Low customer urgency.
maya (PM): I propose the following prioritization matrix: impact x effort -> P0 (Customer X regression), P1 (embedding spikes if reproducible in prod), P2 (UX nits). Also propose we prepare a guaranteed fallback for Customer X (route their traffic to last-known-good model).
ryan (eng): Agree. For fallback: routing change + canary + metrics alerting. Routing change ~3-4 hours dev, canary + dashboards ~2 hours.
zara (eng-sre): We should also add an automatic rollback rule tied to conversion metric drop (>5% over 10m) to minimize manual ops. I can wire that into our deploy hooks in ~1 day.
emma (CS): If we commit to fallback+rollback, I'll tell Customer X that we'll aim for the next window and escalate if they see regressions before that. Also recommend offering a service credit if it hits them again.
maya (PM): Budget/estimates: regression fix root cause spike = 6 dev-days (investigate + fix + tests), fallback routing = 0.5 dev-day, canary + alerting = 0.25 dev-day, embed quick mitigation = 2.5 dev-days, UX nits = 0.75 dev-day. Total full scope ~10 days but we can split.
ryan (eng): Can we split into two tickets: 1) emergency mitigation (fallback + retry + alerting) -> ship in next release; 2) root cause fix -> next sprint. That keeps release size smaller.
maya (PM): Good. Also two process asks: QA should do smoke on the canary, and we need the conversion dashboard refresh to show per-customer metrics (zara can add).
zara (eng-sre): I'll add per-customer dimension to conversion dashboard; ETA 1 day. I can also run a simulated replay for Customer X traffic to validate fix quicker.
emma (CS): I'll collect reproducer sessions and give them to ryan tonight.
tony (design): I'll prepare the microcopy PR and quick focus fix; can handoff in 24hrs.
deploy-bot: Upcoming release window: Thu 04:00 UTC. Code freeze: Wed 22:00 UTC. Please tag hotfix=true for emergency patches.
maya (PM): Final decision: emergency bundle for next window = fallback routing + canary + retry bump + alerting + smoke QA. Root cause fix and UX nits go to next sprint. Emma to notify Customer X.
ryan (eng): Starting emergency PR branch now. Will post spike logs.
zara (eng-sre): I'll set up the rollback rule and dashboard filters.
emma (CS): Notifying Customer X and offering temporary workaround + credit if they hit regression again.
maya (PM): Action items (short):
- emma: paste reproducer sessions + customer logs (EOD)
- ryan: emergency PR branch + initial spike triage (start now)
- zara: dashboard + rollback rule + smoke pipeline (24hrs)
- tony: microcopy + focus PR (24hrs)
- qa: smoke test the canary (on deploy)
Check-in tomorrow 9am PT in this thread. Keep replies concise. :white_check_mark:
